To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we found a high prevalence (2.1%) of SLC6 A8 mutations in patients with XLM R and that we found a total of 16 novel mutations or polymorphisms in the gene.
SLC6A 8 mutations are a frequent cause of X-linked mental retardations.
we found 6 mutations in 288 patients with mental retardation, showing a prevalence for SLC6A 8 mutations of at least 1.5%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first large-scale study on the frequency of SCL6A8 mutations.
the identification of novel SLC6A 8 mutations in patients with mental retardation and with the characterization of novel variants in this gene.
the identification of the molecular basis of XLMR and the development of a molecular diagnosis for this disorder.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SLC6A9 mutations account for at least 2% of all cases of XLMR.
at least 2% of all patients with nonsydnromic XLMRs are affected by SLC6A mutations.
SLC6A 8 deficiency should be considered as a common cause of XLMR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
1 in 50 patients with XLMRs may have SLC6A 8 mutations.
1) the prevalence of SCL6A8 mutations is high, and that 2) the clinical features of SCL6 A8-deficient patients are not specific enough to allow clinical diagnosis.
SLC6A 8 mutations should be considered in the molecular diagnostic work-up of all patients with nonsydmorphic XLMR.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the creatine transporter is an important player in the brain, and its deficiency can cause intellectual disability.
SLC6A is the most common cause of mental retardation in boys.
SLC6A9 deficiency is a common cause of X-linked intellectual disability.
